title: JVM Class File Format
description: The file a compiler emits and a virtual machine refuses to guess about. A magic number, two versions, a constant pool that everything else points into, a string encoding that is not the one it is named after, two offset conventions, a verifier's conclusions written into the file, and an open-ended attribute mechanism that absorbed twenty years of new language features.
author: Underlayer
completion_criteria: Decode a real class file end to end -- header, constant pool, members, code, offsets, stack maps, attributes -- and explain why a format with no section table never needed a new file layout.

concepts.title: Why a Class File
concepts.description: What the format is for, and the four independent implementations every claim in this course is checked against.

concepts.title: The Header and the Fixed Order
concepts.description: Eight bytes, two versions, and a layout that is not the order the source was written in.

concepts.title: The Constant Pool
concepts.description: Twenty tags, one-based indexing, and the two-slot rule that makes some indices permanently unusable.

concepts.title: Modified UTF-8
concepts.description: The encoding CONSTANT_Utf8 actually uses: a two-byte NUL and a six-byte emoji.

concepts.title: Fields, Methods and Descriptors
concepts.description: The descriptor grammar, three separate access-flag tables, and the local slots a long parameter quietly costs two of.

concepts.title: The Code Attribute
concepts.description: max_stack, max_locals, the instruction array, and the nested attributes a method carries inside its own body.

concepts.title: Two Offset Conventions
concepts.description: Branch offsets are relative to the instruction; exception table offsets are absolute. Plus switch padding and the wide prefix.

concepts.title: The Verifier's Data
concepts.description: StackMapTable, why a type checker writes its conclusions into the file, and what the frame types compress.

concepts.title: The Escape Hatch
concepts.description: One generic attribute shape, twenty years of features, and why the file is closed while the attributes are open.

concepts.title: Inner Classes and Nests
concepts.description: The InnerClasses attribute, NestHost and NestMembers, and why the $ in a name is not what it looks like.

concepts.title: The Signature Attribute
concepts.description: Generics as a second, richer type language layered on the erased descriptor.

concepts.title: Annotations
concepts.description: Character-literal type tags, and why every annotation constant is a constant pool index.

concepts.title: Records
concepts.description: The Record attribute and everything the compiler synthesised that the source did not say.

concepts.title: Sealed Types
concepts.description: PermittedSubclasses, and the simplest attribute in the format.

concepts.title: Enums
concepts.description: ACC_ENUM in two flag tables at once, a synthetic field, and two methods nobody wrote.

concepts.title: invokedynamic and Bootstraps
concepts.description: Lambdas as a runtime link, the metafactory, and the instruction that also implements string concatenation.

concepts.title: Modules
concepts.description: The Module attribute, CONSTANT_Module, and the two pool tags javap still calls Unknown.

concepts.title: Version History
concepts.description: What each major version added, and the pattern behind thirty years of additions.
